🚨 BORN BEFORE 1967? YOUR SOCIAL SECURITY COLA TIMING MATTERS!

📘 Claim Every Dollar — The Senior Benefits Playbook: https://marcusretires.com

If you were born in the 1940s, 1950s, or 1960s, your birth year and Social Security eligibility date can affect when cost-of-living adjustments are reflected in your retirement benefits.

In today's Marcus Retires video, we explain the three groups you need to understand before January 2027 — including retirees already receiving benefits, people who are eligible but haven't claimed, and younger Americans approaching Social Security eligibility.

You'll also learn why Medicare deductions can reduce the increase you actually see in your bank account, how Social Security earnings limits work, and why being born on the first day of a month can matter for certain benefit and tax rules.

IN THIS VIDEO:

✅ Group 1: Born in 1961 or earlier — understanding your January benefit adjustment
✅ Group 2: Born in 1962–1964 — how COLAs can affect future retirement benefits before claiming
✅ Group 3: Born in 1965–1966 — why Social Security eligibility timing matters
✅ How Medicare Part B premiums can affect your net payment
✅ What happens when you work while collecting Social Security before full retirement age
✅ The January 1 birthday rule and the additional senior tax deduction
✅ Why Social Security wage indexing and COLAs are different
✅ How to review your Social Security earnings record for errors
✅ Why property taxes and homeowners insurance can still strain a retirement budget

📘 Claim Every Dollar — The Senior Benefits Playbook: https://marcusretires.com

If you were born in the 1940s, 1950s, or 1960s, understanding how Social Security calculates your retirement benefits could make a difference in your financial planning for 2027.

In today's Marcus Retires video, we explain how Social Security cost-of-living adjustments (COLA), birth-year eligibility rules, Medicare Part B deductions, and earnings limits can affect your retirement income.

We also reveal five common household expenses that could consume much of your Social Security increase — and practical steps you can take to review those bills.

THREE SOCIAL SECURITY BIRTH-YEAR GROUPS

1️⃣ Born in 1961 or Earlier

Learn how annual COLA adjustments affect eligible Social Security beneficiaries and why Medicare premiums can change the net amount deposited into your bank account.

2️⃣ Born Between 1962 and 1964

Understand how Social Security COLAs may affect future retirement benefit calculations even if you haven't started collecting benefits.

3️⃣ Born in 1965 or 1966

Discover how age-62 eligibility, wage indexing, and Social Security benefit calculations differ from adjustments applied to older beneficiaries.

✅ Electricity and natural gas bills

✅ Water and sewer charges

✅ Homeowners insurance premiums

✅ Automatic subscriptions and recurring payments

✅ Property taxes and senior homeowner exemptions
